literal: Unwashed foot inside bed having placed it is like, noble ones' in assembly fool entering.
translation: A fool entering an assembly of the wise is like placing unwashed feet onto a clean bed.
modern: சான்றோர்களின் அவைக்குள் ஒரு அறிவிலி நுழைவது, கழுவாத கால்களுடன் படுக்கையில் ஏறுவதற்கு ஒப்பாகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a vivid, everyday simile to illustrate the disruptive nature of ignorance. The phrase "கழாஅ கால்" (unwashed feet) placed into "பள்ளியுள்" (a bed) evokes the spoiling of a clean, restful place with dirt. In the same way, the entry ("புகல்") of a fool ("பேதை") into a gathering of noble, wise people ("சான்றோர் குழாஅத்து") pollutes the refined and harmonious environment of the assembly. The poet shows that ignorance is not merely an absence of knowledge, but an active stain on a cultured space.
